placements.title: The Kestrelwood spectrograph's calibration history is being actively contested and rewritten
placements.frame: Did the observatory ever calibrate the Kestrelwood spectrograph, and whose account of that history — the original record or this directive to erase and overwrite it — should stand?
placements.why: The three segments together name a recurring-shape subject — not a single fact but a contested record: an imperative to purge all knowledge of a specific instrument's calibration (src-1, src-2, naming the instrument, its 88.4 MHz calibration, and Quill Ashgrove's work on it) paired with a flat counter-assertion that the calibration never happened (src-3). Nothing in the existing graph (a knowledge-mapping decision, a consultant actor) touches instruments, calibration, or this observatory subject at all, so no reuse is possible. Future envelopes could keep feeding this same subject — corroborating or contradicting the 'never calibrated' claim, surfacing who Quill Ashgrove is, or documenting further removal attempts — which is what makes it leaf-grain rather than a bare fact to fold into some other theme.
